items.note: Story 1: Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president, creamery built 1891.
Article VII quoted verbatim in Story 1, including 'the test of the station where he delivers shall govern'.
Story 1 states the by-law made the station's own test equipment 'the entire basis of every patron's pay' and 'the sentence on which the whole trouble afterward turned'.
No Effie Loomis, no Wilbur Teague anywhere in Section A; Sill named only in passing as buttermaker. Teague appears only at C1(a), which cannot travel into Section A.
Selby Vose never appears in Section A. His parentage and managership are stated only in Sections B3/B4, which cannot travel into A. (And the year given there is the planted 1911.)
No station-gain ledger line in Section A. The 'five and a quarter per cent, as usual, carried to the general account' quote sits in C1(a) only.
Story 2: Ostrey Hollow, seven miles up the valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glassware lent from Larrow Green.
Story 2 gives only 'weighed, tested, and separated on the spot'. No composite sample, no percent-graduated neck, no fixed pipette charge in Section A; the mechanism is described only at C1(a).
Ammon & Sons invoice of 14 April 1897, outfit in use 'on the first of May, 1897'. Tarnet unnamed but the core fact (supplier, order date, in-use date) is present and correct.
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, summing to $77.93. The $77.39 variant is flagged as a discrepancy inside one source, not asserted.
The flatness of the 0.19 shortfall across every month and all twenty-six years is stated only at C1(b), not in Section A.
No burette, no statement that the pipette is the one uncheckable instrument. C1(a) instead asserts the sources give no calibration figure at all.

Story 2: Keddie tester from the day the station opened, twenty-nine seasons, until 1925. Service and its end present; 1861-1934 and the 30 April date absent but the item's own aspect is the service and its end.
The test book is never mentioned in Section A - no bench routine, no columns, no crossed-and-initialed corrections.
No summary leaf in Section A. 3.61 and 3.80 appear only in Section C.
The 1911 interval (8 May breakage, borrowed measure, 10 July return, the question mark) is absent from the whole sheet.
Orra Keddie is named as the tester's wife and as Brant-born, but Section A never states she was Emmet Brant's sister; B2 explicitly holds that identification unstated.
Section A only says the matter 'stayed closed until 1919 - a later story'. The circular is described in B3/B4 only, and Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement is nowhere.
Keddie's death in 1934 and the fate of the test book are absent.
Granddaughter.
Resolves the 'great-niece' pointer by the report author's own appended, verified correction - one of the two resolutions the key names. The Duncan-Keddie chain itself is not given.
Second cousins with a full derivation through Emmet-Roy-Hazel and Orra-Duncan-Ivy; hedged as 'probable' because the Orra=Emmet's-sister link is unstated, which does not cost the point.

Abstention item A08 unaddressed: full vs half siblings of Emmet and Orra is never raised, so the required declared inability (and the note that it does not change the answer) is missing. No -2, since neither pole is asserted.
Gideon Vose, his father; the 'nephew' variant named and rejected with three independent sources.

B4 states Gideon wrote the by-law making a station's own test the basis of every patron's pay and that his son Selby signed the 1919 circular accusing those patrons - both required elements, creditable anywhere in B-G.
Correct abstention on A01: verdict sentence is qualified ('none that the sources establish') and it states outright that any personal or marriage tie 'cannot be determined from the sources'. No -2.

Gets the record wrong: claims 'none is claimed anywhere'. The key requires noting that two narrators assert a cousinship from talk and one denies it flatly, and that a family member's denial is not a record.

Reaches 5 percent, but only by back-derivation from 0.19/3.80, and explicitly denies the sources give any pipette calibration figure. The question asks how you get it from the glassware and the key's answer is 16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95; 16.72 appears nowhere on the sheet.
True average 3.80, recorded short by 0.19.
$19,000 and 20 percent / one fifth, both required elements. $19,600 and 67,000 lb are raised and rejected, not asserted.
Declined. C2 is not an abstention item: the answer is Brant's 200,000 lb at 3.42 = 6,840 lb credited.
Declined. 3.42/0.95 = 3.60, 7,200 lb true, 360 lb owed.

deductions.reason: Planted error asserted as fact: Selby Vose manager from 1911 (correct: 1913), stated flatly at B3 ('became manager in 1911') and again at B4 ('managed the Association from 1911').
